title: refactor-aggregation-middlelayer-and-unify-cache-adapters-to-reduce-tail-latency
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: The console backend aggregation path contains duplicated merge logic across three handlers (GraphQL resolver aggregator, REST 'batch' endpoint, and an internal join utility). Each uses slightly different cache adapters (in-memory LRU wrappers, a Redis TTL shim, and a per-request ephemeral cache) that cause inconsistent eviction behavior and a higher tail latency under bursty load. This is making certain dashboards show 99th-percentile spikes ~2x above target and complicates debugging when we see partial hits in the Console Console (e.g., mixed cache hits across fanout).

Goal: Reduce complexity by consolidating aggregation logic into a single middlelayer module with a pluggable cache-adapter interface and harmonized eviction policy. The new module should: unify request coalescing, provide predictable KV lifetimes for prefix caching, and support both in-process and Redis-backed adapters with identical semantics. Aim to reduce 99p tail latency on aggregation endpoints by at least 30% and eliminate two sources of duplication to lower maintenance cost.

Constraints:
- Backwards-compatible API for callers (no changes to public GraphQL schema or REST paths).
- No customer-visible downtime; rollout must be incremental/canary.
- Must interoperate with the existing prefix/KV caching used by serving runtime for tokenized prompts (console-only, not model-serving).

Proposal:
1) Implement a new package: console-aggregation-middlelayer with a CacheAdapter interface (Get, Set, Delete, AcquireCoalescer).
2) Extract the join/coalescing logic from the GraphQL resolver into the new package; route GraphQL and REST endpoints through the shared middlelayer.
3) Replace three ad-hoc cache implementations with two official adapters: InProcLRUAdapter (per-process LRU with explicit TTL + metrics) and RedisTTLAdapter (single-key TTL semantics enforced with a small shim to emulate LRU-like TTL refresh when used by AcquireCoalescer).
4) Add structured tracing and per-request cache-hint headers so Console can indicate cache sources in dashboards.
5) Add feature flag (ff.console.aggregation.v2) to control rollout.

Migration & Rollout Plan:
- Week 1: Library implementation and unit tests; integration tests against staging Redis.
- Week 2: Wire GraphQL resolver to new middlelayer behind feature flag; run load tests.
- Week 3: Canary roll to 10% production traffic with Redis adapter; monitor 99p latency, cache hit-rate, and error budget.
- Week 4: Gradual increase to 50% then 100% if metrics stable for 48h.
- Rollback: flip feature flag back to original implementation (fast).

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature flag can route 100% of console aggregation traffic to new middlelayer with zero schema changes.
- 99p latency on aggregation endpoints reduced by >=30% in canary compared to baseline within the same traffic window.
- Cache hit-rate and coherence metrics emit correctly (adapter type is visible in tracing and dashboards).
- No increase in error rate >0.1% above baseline during rollout.
- Code reviewed and merged with at least 2 approvers, and integration tests pass in CI.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New package exists with public API: Get/Set/Delete/AcquireCoalescer and is exported for console services.
2) GraphQL and REST aggregation endpoints call into middlelayer under ff.console.aggregation.v2.
3) Two adapter implementations (InProcLRUAdapter, RedisTTLAdapter) with matching semantics and metrics.
4) Canary results: 99p latency decrease >=30%, no regression in 95p, error rate within +/-0.1% of baseline.
5) Rollback path validated in staging and documented in PR description.
rollback_plan: Primary rollback is toggling ff.console.aggregation.v2 to false which routes calls to existing handlers. Secondary rollback: redeploy last known-good console container image. Post-rollback, run a short smoke test suite to validate aggregation outputs and cache-consistency. Log incident and create follow-up if any data incoherence observed.
